title: Aviation Daily Brief
headline: The FAA has ruled the 737 MAX flight-computer glitch not a safety concern, putting MAX 10 certification back on track for Ryanair and Alaska.
summary: An FAA review board found the U14 flight-management software issue on some 737 MAX jets not safety-critical; Leeham now sees MAX 10 certification back on track.
Air cargo is heading into peak season on rising rates: Hong Kong-North America averaged $7.02/kg in September, 31% up on a year earlier, with jet fuel more than 100% higher year on year.
airBaltic plans 500-700 job cuts, a smaller A220-300 fleet and more ACMI capacity under a new business plan.
Boeing's $14.7 billion seeker contract from Lockheed Martin funds a seven-year plan to triple PAC-3 MSE seeker production.

sections.title: Safety & regulation
sections.takeaway: The MAX 10's late software scare has been closed by the regulator itself.

items.headline: FAA board clears 737 MAX flight-computer software issue
items.so_what: With the U14 flight-management glitch judged not safety-critical, the MAX 10 can join the MAX 7 in clearing its last regulatory hurdle - capacity Ryanair and Alaska Airlines have on order.
items.detail: The glitch can occur when pilots load a new flight plan for a go-around. The FAA's Corrective Action Review Board concluded on October 2 that pilots retain full control and the indications are clear; Alaska had expected certification by the end of September.

sources.title: Boeing's Path to Max 10 Certification Looks Clear Again

sections.title: Airlines
sections.takeaway: Premium capacity up at British Airways, headcount down at airBaltic, and cargo yields rising into the peak.

items.headline: British Airways turns 75% of its A380 seats premium
items.so_what: All 12 BA A380s are being refitted with more than 35,000 parts each, shifting the type towards premium cabins as part of a £7 billion transformation plan.
items.detail: BA says punctuality is at levels not seen since 2012, with Q3 2026 its best ever departure punctuality within 15 minutes at Heathrow.

sources.title: Fewer seats, more luxury: step into the new British Airways A380 interiors

items.headline: airBaltic to cut 500-700 roles and shrink its A220-300 fleet
items.so_what: 500-700 of about 3,000 staff go as the carrier leans on year-round ACMI partners instead of its own aircraft - less Baltic capacity under its own operation.
items.detail: Unions are being consulted on reduced workloads for pilots and cabin crew; the new structures for the rest of the business are due by mid-October.

sources.title: airBaltic plans up to 700 job cuts as it reshapes business

items.headline: Air freight rates edge up into the fourth-quarter peak
items.so_what: Hong Kong-North America averaged $7.02/kg in September (31% up year on year) and Hong Kong-Europe $4.80/kg (up 8.8%); the Baltic Air Freight Index jumped 5% in the week to October 5.
items.detail: TAC Index attributes the year-on-year rise to jet fuel prices more than 100% higher and to data-centre demand to the US; the EU's €3 charge on low-value parcels is weighing on Asia-Europe volumes.

sources.title: Airfreight rates edge up in September

items.headline: Delta recovers from a global technology issue
items.so_what: Delta says systems are stabilising after a limited issue with data connectivity to some systems; the scale of any disruption is not stated.

sections.title: Manufacturers & supply chain
sections.takeaway: A new regional-aircraft assembly line opens in Germany.

items.headline: Deutsche Aircraft opens D328eco final assembly in Leipzig
items.so_what: The more than €100 million site is designed for up to 48 aircraft a year and moves the D328eco from development to serial production.

sources.title: Deutsche Aircraft opens Leipzig plant for D328eco production

sections.title: Defence & space
sections.takeaway: Missile-defence demand reaches the supply chain, and Northrop flies its own collaborative combat aircraft.

items.headline: Boeing wins $14.7 billion to triple PAC-3 MSE seeker output
items.so_what: A seven-year plan to triple seeker production for Lockheed Martin's Patriot interceptor, after seeker deliveries already rose more than 30% in 2025.
items.detail: Work starts while final terms, including pricing, are negotiated; Boeing has invested more than $200 million in its Huntsville seeker production since 2024.

sources.title: Boeing wins $14.7 billion contract to triple Patriot missile seeker production

items.headline: Northrop's YFQ-48A Talon Blue flies fully autonomously
items.so_what: An internally funded CCA flying taxi to landing on its own, as the US Air Force targets 500 autonomous aircraft in service by 2032 - though Northrop has no CCA production contract yet.

sources.title: Northrop Grumman's YFQ-48A CCA completes first fully autonomous flight

items.headline: Morocco's first F-16 Block 72 flies; first full-rate MH-139A order
items.so_what: Two US programmes advance: Morocco's first F-16 Block 72 is in flight test towards first delivery, and the MH-139A's first four full-rate helicopters take the total under contract to 42.
items.detail: Boeing has delivered 27 MH-139As. In Morocco, an MRO facility of more than 8,000 m² at Benslimane, with Maintenance Aero Maroc, is to service C-130s and later F-16s.

sources.title: Lockheed Martin Announces First Flight of Morocco's First F 16 Block 72
Boeing wins first full-rate MH-139A Grey Wolf order

sections.title: Sustainability
sections.takeaway: Airlines want CORSIA, not the EU ETS, to be the global carbon framework.

items.headline: IATA marks ten years of CORSIA as the EU reviews its ETS
items.so_what: More than 130 countries take part and CORSIA should have mitigated about 200 million tonnes of CO2 by year-end; IATA wants the EU's ETS review - which considers covering destinations within 5,000 km - to reinforce CORSIA, not overlap it.
items.detail: From 2027 CORSIA is estimated to cover about 85% of global emissions, with up to $120 billion in climate finance over the life of the scheme.

sources.title: Ten Years on from CORSIA Agreement, Governments Must Strengthen the Global Framework for Aviation Emissions

How much capacity moves to ACMI partners.
Whether rates keep pace with jet fuel.
A 5,000 km scope would overlap CORSIA on long-haul routes.
